title: Designing a feature
description: Turn a rough idea into a reviewed spec before a single line of code is written

steps.title: Start the brainstorming skill
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Classifies your request as a spike (feasibility question), bounded (small change to existing code), or architectural (new project or restructuring), and says which out loud so you can override. Then asks questions one at a time to understand purpose, constraints, and success criteria.
steps.whatToExpect: A one-line classification, then 1–6 questions depending on the path. For a bounded change you get a short design in chat. For architectural work Claude proposes 2–3 approaches and may offer a browser-based visual companion for mockups.

steps.title: Answer Claude's questions
steps.instruction: No command needed — just reply in the terminal.
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Asks one question at a time, preferring multiple choice. For architectural work it proposes 2–3 approaches with trade-offs and a recommendation, then presents the design section by section.
steps.whatToExpect: Claude asks for approval after each design section. Nothing is implemented until you say yes, even for a two-sentence bounded design.

steps.title: Approve the design spec
steps.instruction: Review each section and say yes, or ask for changes.
steps.whatClaudeDoes: For architectural work, saves the approved spec to docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md, self-reviews it for placeholders and contradictions, asks you to review the file, then invokes writing-plans. Bounded work skips the spec and goes straight to implementation.
steps.whatToExpect: After approval, Claude writes an implementation plan where each task has its own test cycle and bite-sized 2–5 minute steps.

title: Building a feature
description: Implement with TDD and subagent-driven development — Claude works autonomously through each task

steps.title: Create an isolated workspace
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Creates a new git branch and isolated worktree so your feature work won't contaminate the main workspace. Runs project setup and verifies a clean test baseline.
steps.whatToExpect: A new branch is created. Claude confirms the test baseline is clean before work starts.

steps.title: Build with subagent-driven development
steps.instruction: Type this in Claude Code (after an approved plan exists):
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Dispatches a fresh implementer subagent per task from your plan. After each task a task reviewer checks spec compliance and code quality; findings loop back for up to five fix rounds. When all tasks are done, a whole-branch review runs before handing off to finishing-a-development-branch.
steps.whatToExpect: Claude works through each task in the plan and picks the cheapest model that fits each role. You will see progress updates. It stops to ask only when a decision is genuinely yours to make.

steps.title: TDD is enforced automatically
steps.instruction: No action needed — this triggers during implementation.
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Enforces RED→GREEN→REFACTOR: writes a failing test first, confirms it fails, writes minimal code to pass it, then refactors. Deletes any code written before the test.
steps.whatToExpect: Every feature gets a test written before implementation. Claude won't commit code that doesn't pass its tests.

title: Debugging
description: Find root cause systematically — not by guessing and hoping

steps.title: Start systematic debugging
steps.instruction: Type this in Claude Code when you hit a bug:
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Runs a 4-phase root cause process: (1) Root cause investigation — read errors fully, reproduce, check recent changes, trace bad data to its source, (2) Pattern analysis — compare against working code, (3) Hypothesis and testing — one specific hypothesis, tested with the smallest change, (4) Implementation — write a failing test, apply a single fix, verify.
steps.whatToExpect: Claude will not propose a fix until it has evidence identifying the root cause. If three fixes fail it stops and questions the architecture instead of trying a fourth.

steps.title: Verify the fix actually works
steps.instruction: Type this after applying a fix:
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Runs actual verification commands and confirms the output before claiming the bug is fixed. Prevents 'it should work now' without proof.
steps.whatToExpect: Claude shows you real command output confirming the fix works — not just a claim that it does.

title: Code review
description: Request and respond to reviews the right way — with technical rigor, not rubber-stamping

steps.title: Request a code review
steps.instruction: Type this in Claude Code after writing code:
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Dispatches a code-reviewer subagent with the plan and the commit range. The reviewer reports strengths, issues, and recommendations, with issues sorted by severity: Critical, Important, Minor.
steps.whatToExpect: A structured review report. Critical issues are fixed immediately, Important ones before proceeding, Minor ones are noted for later. Claude pushes back with reasoning if the reviewer is wrong.

steps.title: Respond to review feedback
steps.instruction: Type this after receiving review feedback:
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Processes review feedback with technical rigor — verifies each suggestion is actually correct before implementing. Pushes back on incorrect feedback rather than blindly applying it.
steps.whatToExpect: Claude confirms which feedback is valid, explains which it disagrees with (and why), and implements accepted changes with verification.

title: Merging & shipping
description: Wrap up a development branch cleanly — merge, PR, or keep

steps.title: Finish the development branch
steps.instruction: Type this when all tasks are complete and tests pass:
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Verifies all tests pass, then presents three options: (1) Merge locally into the base branch, (2) Push and open a pull request, (3) Keep the branch as-is for later. Discards the work only if you ask. Cleans up the git worktree after your choice.
steps.whatToExpect: A clear decision point with context on each option. Claude won't merge until it confirms tests are passing.

title: Understanding a skill
description: Deep-dive into any superpowers skill — when to use it, how it works, what to type

steps.title: Browse the skill library
steps.instruction: Click the link below or search by skill name:
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Not applicable — this scenario links directly to the skill browser.
steps.whatToExpect: Every skill listed by category: Planning, Building, Testing, Debugging, Review, Git, Meta. Start with using-superpowers, the entry point that decides when the others are invoked.

steps.title: Click any skill for full details
steps.whatToExpect: The slash command to invoke it, when to use it (specific triggers), how it works step-by-step, and which scenarios use it.

title: Writing a custom skill
description: Create your own skills for project-specific workflows — extend superpowers for your domain

steps.title: Start the writing-skills guide
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Walks you through creating a new skill following superpowers best practices. Covers skill structure, writing clear trigger conditions, and testing methodology including adversarial pressure testing.
steps.whatToExpect: A guided process for designing, writing, and testing a custom skill. Personal skills live in ~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md and are available immediately.

steps.title: Test the skill
steps.instruction: No separate command — testing is part of the writing-skills process.
steps.whatClaudeDoes: Runs adversarial pressure testing: tries to find prompts that should trigger the skill but don't, and prompts that should not trigger it but do. Iterates until the skill behaves reliably.
steps.whatToExpect: A skill that triggers consistently in the right situations and stays out of the way when it shouldn't apply.
